Commons gives 1 January 1959, but the embedded tag gives only the year. The dated 9/59 sleeve is a release-carrier date, not a session date. No day or month is adopted without session documentation.

The original issue identifies the recording collaboration with Polskie Nagrania in Warsaw; a particular hall is not documented in this source.

[1]
Transfer
Unknown Unknown

The original recording credits name Heinz Wildhagen (recording engineer) and Hans Weber (recording supervisor). They are not documented as the transfer or restoration staff for this FLAC.

[5] [3]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

No transfer date is documented; upload and encoding-software dates are not session or transfer dates.

[1] [3]
Processing
Embedded encoder: libFLAC 1.3.2 20170101. Commons master: FLAC, 16-bit, 44.1 kHz, 2 channels. Documented

These are file properties, not evidence of noise reduction, equalisation, pitch correction or other restoration. Earlier processing is not documented.

[3]
Composition rights
Original composition is public domain in ordinary life-plus-70 jurisdictions. Inferred, not documented

The composer died in 1943. Rights in the 1959 recording are separate; this is not a worldwide clearance for every edition.

[6] [7]
Recording rights
Rule 3 — territorial: sound recording public domain in the European Union (pre-1963 publication basis). Documented

Commons applies PD-EU-audio to Richter/Wisłocki’s DG recording attributed to 1959. Usable under the programme’s pre-1963 European sound-recording rule; the former 50-year term had expired before the 2013 extension. This is territorial, not a worldwide licence; US sound-recording status is not established. A recording date alone is not represented as an independently verified first-publication date.
